title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 1st District
area: Western Massachusetts, including Springfield, Pittsfield, and the Berkshires

context.text: Incumbent Richard Neal defeated Jeromie Whalen, a Belchertown schoolteacher, in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary, 55.2% to 44.8%. No Republican candidate appeared on the primary ballot.

summary.text: Richard Neal is the Democratic incumbent, a former Springfield high school teacher, city councilor and mayor who has been in the U.S. House since 1989. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee, which he chaired from 2019 to 2023 and on which he is now the ranking Democrat. He won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born in Worcester, Massachusetts, in 1949, and raised and educated in Springfield.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from American International College and a master's degree in public administration from the Barney School of Business and Public Administration at the University of Hartford.
Before entering Congress, worked as a high school teacher.
Worked as an assistant to Springfield Mayor William C. Sullivan beginning in 1973.
Served on the Springfield City Council, to which he was elected in 1978, and as Mayor of Springfield from 1984 to 1988.
First elected to the U.S. House in 1988; represented Massachusetts's 2nd District from 1989 to 2013 and the redrawn 1st District since 2013.
Served his first two terms on the House Banking Committee before joining the Ways and Means Committee in 1993.

Elected Chairman of Ways and Means in January 2019, which his official biography describes as the first time since 1875 that a Massachusetts representative held the post; chaired the committee from 2019 to 2023 and has been its ranking member since January 2023.
Is the Democratic leader of the Friends of Ireland Caucus and, according to his official biography, traveled to Ireland in 1994 to observe the first IRA ceasefire.

According to his official biography, is dean of the Massachusetts and New England congressional delegations and has received honorary degrees from institutions including Mount Holyoke College, Springfield College, Ulster University and Queen's University Belfast.

priorities.text: "I've fought tirelessly for policies that make a difference for hard-working families and future generations: fairer taxes, affordable and accessible healthcare, taking on climate change, preserving Social Security, and more."

Campaign statement: fighting "back against Donald Trump and Republicans' reckless budget that slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy and add trillions to the deficit."

positions.summary: Campaign describes fighting a Republican budget he says "slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy."
positions.quote: fighting back against Donald Trump and Republicans' reckless budget that slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy and add trillions to the deficit

positions.summary: Campaign material frames his record as pursuing "fairer taxes" and opposing tax breaks for the wealthy.
Cites "taking on climate change" among his record in Congress.

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Ways and Means Committee.
Statement on House passage of a War Powers Resolution following U.S. strikes in Iran, saying Congress "reminded the President and the nation who the power to declare war rests with."

candidates.name: Nadia Milleron

summary.text: Nadia Milleron is an attorney, small business owner and aviation-safety advocate running as an unenrolled candidate. She became active in public advocacy after her daughter died in the 2019 Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 MAX crash, and she previously ran against Rep. Neal in 2024. She describes her campaign as independent of party and focused on accountability, term limits and affordability.

background.text: Born in Berkeley, California, and graduated from Berkeley High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Smith College (1986) and a law degree from the University of Iowa (1994).

Career experience includes working as an attorney and small business owner. She describes beginning her legal career representing children in contested family-court cases and, often pro bono, patients at a state mental hospital in probate court.

Her 24-year-old daughter, Samya Stumo, died in the March 2019 Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crash. She and her husband filed a wrongful-death suit against Boeing, and a jury awarded the family $49.5 million in damages on May 13, 2026, according to Wikipedia.

Describes herself as having helped pass the bipartisan Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act in 2020 and as having worked with Illinois legislators to change a state law she says protected corporations over victims.
Ran as an unenrolled candidate for Massachusetts's 1st District in 2024 and lost to Richard Neal in the November 5, 2024 general election (Neal 62.4%).
Is running again in 2026 as an unenrolled candidate and has pledged, on her campaign website, to serve no more than six years if elected.
